accepted_examples.german: Darf ich für eine Weile das Telefon benutzen?
accepted_examples.english: May I use the telephone for a while?
accepted_examples.note: The sentence directly uses Telefon for a telephone.

accepted_examples.german: Sagen Sie mir, was Ihr Plan ist.
accepted_examples.note: Plan is used as a proposed course of action.

accepted_examples.german: Ich komme so oft hierher, wie ich kann.
accepted_examples.english: I come here as often as I can.
accepted_examples.note: This clearly shows movement or direction to this place.

accepted_examples.german: Ich habe auf der Straße einen Dollar gefunden.
accepted_examples.english: I found a dollar in the street.
accepted_examples.note: Dollar refers to one unit of currency.

accepted_examples.german: Stell das Glas nicht zu nah an die Tischkante.
accepted_examples.english: Don't put the glass near the edge of the table.
accepted_examples.note: nah describes spatial proximity to the table edge.

accepted_examples.german: Nicht die Menge macht's, sondern die Qualität.
accepted_examples.english: It is quality, not quantity that counts.
accepted_examples.note: Menge means quantity in this contrast.

accepted_examples.german: Das hier ist dein Schirm. Wo ist meiner?
accepted_examples.note: meiner is a substantival possessive pronoun meaning mine.

accepted_examples.german: Tom drehte sich, als er Mary rufen hörte.
accepted_examples.english: Tom turned when he heard Mary shout.
accepted_examples.note: rufen is used for calling or shouting aloud.

accepted_examples.german: Ich habe leider gerade zu viel zu tun.
accepted_examples.english: Unfortunately, I'm too busy right now.

accepted_examples.german: Warum ist das Leben so voll mit Leiden?
accepted_examples.english: Why is life so full of suffering?
accepted_examples.note: voll expresses being full of or filled with something.

accepted_examples.german: Ich weiß nicht, was aus ihm geworden ist.
accepted_examples.english: I don't know what has become of him.
accepted_examples.note: geworden is the Partizip II of werden, used here with sein.

held_examples.german: Dieser Ort ist am Arsch der Welt.
held_examples.reason: This idiom means a remote place, not the target body-part sense.
This is a stative belonging/location use and is less direct for the target directional meaning 'to here'.

held_examples.german: Alles in allem ist er ein guter Lehrer.
held_examples.reason: This is a fixed idiom meaning all things considered; it does not clearly teach allem as a productive dative form.

held_examples.german: Das war, alles in allem, gar nicht schlecht.
held_examples.reason: This is a fixed idiom meaning all in all; it does not clearly teach allem as a productive dative form.

held_examples.german: Ich darf Sie ohne Pass nicht hereinlassen.
held_examples.reason: Pass means a permit or document here, not a mountain pass.

held_examples.german: Tom fing einen Pass ab, der für Johannes bestimmt war.
held_examples.reason: Pass means a sports pass here, not a mountain pass.

held_examples.german: Es hat uns noch nie jemand Geld gegeben.
held_examples.reason: This uses gegeben as a verbal participle, while the entry targets adjectival given.

held_examples.german: Ich habe Tom schon zu viele Chancen gegeben.
held_examples.reason: This uses gegeben as a verbal participle, while the entry targets adjectival given.

held_examples.german: Ich habe hier alle Hände voll zu tun.
held_examples.reason: This is an idiom meaning to be busy, rather than the target full/filled sense.

held_examples.german: Dieser Film ist es wert, gesehen zu werden.
held_examples.reason: Film means a movie here, not a thin layer.

held_examples.german: Sie drehten den Film in einer wirklichen Wüste.
held_examples.reason: Film means a movie here, not a thin layer.

editorial_examples.note: A concise sentence for the colloquial body-part sense; checked against Duden's Arsch entry.

editorial_examples.german: Mit allem, was du gesagt hast, bin ich einverstanden.
editorial_examples.english: I agree with everything you said.
editorial_examples.note: mit governs the dative; allem is the target inflected pronoun form.

editorial_examples.german: Der Pass war wegen des Schnees gesperrt.
editorial_examples.english: The mountain pass was closed because of the snow.
editorial_examples.note: Pass is unambiguously a mountain pass in this context.

editorial_examples.german: Unter den gegebenen Umstaänden ist eine Änderung nötig.
editorial_examples.english: Under the given circumstances, a change is necessary.
editorial_examples.note: This uses gegeben as an attributive adjective meaning given; Duden confirms the adjectival participle use.

editorial_examples.german: Ein dünner Film aus Staub bedeckte die Oberfläche.
editorial_examples.english: A thin film of dust covered the surface.
editorial_examples.note: Film refers to a thin continuous layer, not a movie.

entry_updates.note: Duden conjugation lists geworden as the Partizip II of the full verb werden.
The entry is an inflected verb form, not an adjective; link it to its base lemma werden.

entry_updates.value: Inflected form: Partizip II of werden; combines with sein (for example, ist geworden).
entry_updates.note: Replaces the adjective-only usage note with the checked participle pattern.

inflected_links.form_note: Partizip II of werden (become); used with sein.

plural_reviews.note: Duden gives Ladys as the plural for the general common-noun use; its aristocratic title sense is marked without plural.
Weisen is the plural for Weise meaning way or manner.
Geister is the plural for Geist in the sense spirit.
Boote is the standard plural.
The plural is Colonels; the candidate incorrectly included the unchanged singular Colonel.
Nachrichten meaning news broadcasts is used only in the plural; singular Nachricht is a separate message/news-item sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: This entry refers to news broadcasts or news bulletins and is plural-only. A singular Nachricht means an individual message or piece of news.

plural_reviews.note: Frieden is the listed plural, but Duden marks the common abstract peace sense as usually singular and without plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: For the abstract state of peace, German normally uses singular Frieden. The plural Frieden is possible but rare and sense-dependent.

plural_reviews.note: Gerichte is the plural for Gericht meaning court of justice.
Standard usage normally treats das Weihnachten as singular; the same form occurs in plural expressions and regional plural use.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Weihnachten is usually neuter singular in standard usage. The same form is also used as a plural in set phrases such as fröhliche Weihnachten and in regional usage.

plural_reviews.note: The unit Henry has an unchanged written plural.

plural_reviews.value: No regular plural in the sleep-state sense
plural_reviews.note: Schlaf meaning the state of sleep has no regular plural; Schläfe is a different feminine noun meaning temple.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Schlaf meaning the state of sleeping is normally singular-only. Schläfe means temple and is a separate noun, not its plural.

plural_reviews.note: Haare is the usual plural for countable hairs; hair as a mass can also be used in the singular.
The plural is rare and does not describe ordinary general past usage.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Vergangenheit is normally singular when it means the past in general. Vergangenheiten is rare and refers to distinct historical pasts or technical contexts.

plural_reviews.note: Sheriffs is the standard plural.
Schicksale is the standard plural.

plural_reviews.value: No regular plural in the abstract intellect sense
plural_reviews.note: Duden's common intellect sense is used as an abstract noun and gives no regular plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Verstand meaning the ability to think or reason is normally singular-only.

plural_reviews.note: Borde is the plural for Bord meaning a shelf or board fixed to a wall.
Gläser is the count plural for drinking vessels; unchanged Glas is used as a measure expression and as a rare material plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: For countable drinking vessels, use Gläser. The unchanged form Glas appears in measure expressions such as zwei Glas Wein; the material plural is rare.

plural_reviews.note: Bänder is the plural for a strip, tape or ribbon; Bande belongs to other Band senses such as bonds or fetters.
Messer is unchanged in the plural for the agent noun meaning a person who measures.
